summary.intent: Drive the Callisto repo toward v1: ship the unblocked refactors and fixes as stacked PRs with real-tool verification, prepare the 0.10.3 release, then implement the second W3 PR (sealed Python file sets with strict digests).
summary.outcome: Shipped R5a/R5b/SYS-NAPI, R3, R1, SYS-BARRIER and review-fix PRs, and 0.10.3 published. Sealed Python file sets are implemented with a build-python job, artifact-manifest --seal-python, and strict E307 digest checks. `just ci` passes at 92.76% coverage, and the review fixes were committed and pushed. The PR was not confirmed opened and the hosted workflow has not run.

repo: Release flow is plan/build/execute, and only execute gets registry secrets. Recovery has no journal: it re-derives operations and observes the remote, with ProviderObservationV1 values Absent, Exact, Conflict and Indeterminate.

The release test harness allow-lists every external git/tool call (TOOL_SHAPES in release_harness.rs). A new git invocation such as `git show -s --format=%ct HEAD` needs an allow-list entry and a real-git probe in provider_flag_contract_tests.rs.
An architecture test forbids hand-rolled manifest parsing outside the model and manifests crates. Use IdentityIndex::native_name and read_identity.
AGENTS.md and memory forbid session links in commits and PRs. It also wants one copy of helpers (is_wheel/is_sdist are currently duplicated) and a record for deliberately deferred items.

Generated workflows are linted with actionlint and zizmor, and rendered template bytes are pinned by insta snapshots (init/tests.rs). The generated build-matrix workflow is only produced for binaries or platform packages, so Python-only repos keep the single-job workflow.
The intent omits artifactSlots when empty, so jq `.artifactSlots[]` iterates null. The macOS bash used by the generated workflow lacks `mapfile`, so a portable loop is needed.

PyPI behavior: re-uploading identical bytes returns 200, different bytes under the same name return 400, yank is release-level, new files are rejected after 14 days, and the simple index caches for 600s. Twine uploads sequentially and aborts at the first failure.

code.finding: The strict digest compare treated an index entry with no sha256 as equal (`is_some_and(|d| d != ...)`). This contradicts the sealed guarantee, so the review fix treats a missing hash as differing for sealed sets.
`publish` uploaded sealed files without re-hashing, so a swap after the verify step went undetected until `confirm`. The fix re-hashes right before building the upload argv.
`git show -s --format=%ct HEAD` breaks under log.showSignature with a signed HEAD, so it needs `--no-show-signature`.

workflow: Write the failing test first, then run a mutation check (revert part of the fix) to prove characterization snapshots catch regressions before refactoring.
Measure line coverage of the function being split and add characterization tests for unexecuted branches before moving code.
Use independent subagent reviews on risky changes. They found real defects in #202 and in the sealed-set work. Subagent hand-backs are not user input and need checking.
Verify with real tools (real cargo/gh/git, twine against pypiserver) because fake-tool harnesses let the 0.10.1 regression through.
The sandbox rejects heredocs and inline scripts mentioning git, BSD sed patterns and some cd/xargs forms. Work around with script files in the scratchpad or the Edit tool.
Agent idle_notification results truncate near 4000 characters, so request reports again via SendMessage.

friction: The first stack PR (#205) conflicted after #202 merged and edited a test block that #205 moved. This needed merges upward through the stack.
Sandbox and permission refusals: heredocs, git inside inline Python, and the auto-mode classifier denying batch worktree removal.
I misreported #210 as still waiting on checks when the user had already merged it.
I spawned a pointless 'noop' agent that produced a confusing hand-back while the real review was still running.
GitHub timed out on `gh release list` and `git fetch`, so the 0.10.3 tags could not be confirmed at one point.
The first negative-control script tripped an unrelated repository-mismatch guard and proved nothing, so it had to be redone.
The first `just ci` runs failed on formatting and a stray blank line, and the e2e shims served empty hashes that sealed mode now rejects.
Several of my earlier claims were disproved by real-tool checks (uv stale pins, reproducibility, yank scope, build location).
open_items: The sealed-set PR was committed and pushed, but the transcript does not confirm it was opened or reviewed. #231 and #232 are awaiting user review and merge.
Python-only repos stay unsealed because they use the single-job workflow. Sealing them would need the CI route, so this is the user's decision.
Sealing is opt-in on the execute side (review F3). Document it as a deliberate deferral, or add a --require-sealed-python flag.
The 14-day upload-window warning is left out because the provider context has no clock.
The hosted workflow has not run, and the generated execute job still needs twine on PATH.
`build_python_distributions` builds twice if one package has two PyPI publishes. The is_wheel/is_sdist helpers are duplicated across artifact.rs and pypi_files.rs.
A fresh run after a partial upload rebuilds every file, so E307 fires on any non-bit-identical file.
W9/D01 owner wire and migration choices, W11 hosted verification, and previous-tag-templates for renames are still open.
Python dependency groups are deferred and recorded in docs/publishing.md.
Stale worktrees (stack-ci, wave1-stack, wave2-base, wave1-base, w2-sys-retry, owner-history, locked fix-gh-credentials) and W0 branch deletion need the user's per-branch confirmation.
SYS-BARRIER #213 and R1 #214 were open, and the real-tool attestation note on #216 was not posted.
Follow-ups to consider: uv build and uv publish as defaults, trusted publishing (OIDC), persisting the manifest in the GitHub release, and a longer index-lag confirmation window.
